fact_en: A butterfly starts life as an egg, hatches into a leaf-eating caterpillar, becomes a pupa, and finally comes out with beautiful wings!
fact_bis: Ang alibangbang magsugod isip itlog, mahimong tangkong nga mokaon og dahon, dayon mahimong pupa, ug sa kataposan mogawas nga adunay nindot nga pako!

findings.note: EN: "hatches into a leaf-eating caterpillar"; tl correctly says "higad". The Cebuano names the larval stage "tangkong" - water spinach (kangkong) - so the card reads "the butterfly becomes a tangkong that eats leaves, then a pupa", naming a vegetable as the life-cycle stage, and nothing in the card (title is just "Siklo sa Alibangbang") corrects it. Corpus evidence: "tangkong" occurs on only 2 cards, both caterpillar contexts (this one and ffct-11068 "itlog, tangkong, pupa, alibangbang"), while the corpus otherwise uses "ulod" for caterpillar (e.g. ffct-03849 "Ulod sa Alibangbang", ffct-03765) and spells the vegetable "kangkong" on 22 cards. Medium confidence - narrow grep (2 cards), both the same defect.

fact_en:
What's really inside a wasp's sting?

It's not just one substance! Wasp venom is a mix of chemicals and proteins that cause pain and swelling — that's why the sting burns right away.
fact_bis:
Unsa gyud ang sulod sa hilo sa putyukan?

Dili lang usa ka butang ang hilo sa putyukan. Sagol kini sa lain-laing kemikal ug protina nga maghatag og kasakit ug paghubag — mao nga mura'g nagdilaab human matusok.

findings.note: EN is about WASP venom ("What's really inside a wasp's sting?"); the Cebuano body says "hilo sa putyukan" twice, and putyukan is the honeybee. Corpus proof, no Cebuano intuition needed: ffct-03517 renders "Wasps and hornets don't make honey - honey comes only from honeybees" as "Ang putakti ug hornet dili maghimo og dugos - ang tam-is nga dugos gikan ra sa putyukan", i.e. the corpus itself uses putakti=wasp vs putyukan=bee; putyukan appears on 90 cards, overwhelmingly for "bee" (beekeepers, queen bee, honey, pollination). The tl of this same card says "putakti", so the Cebuano is the divergent one. A Cebuano-only child learns this is bee venom. Same swap recurs on ffct-00767, ffct-01283, ffct-02130, ffct-03099 (corpus elsewhere uses tambuboan/tambubuk for wasp), so the grep is worth running.

fact_en:
Why does a stranded jellyfish look like wet plastic?

A cnidarian has no bones and a soft, jelly-like body that's mostly water — that's why it looks like a wet blob on the beach.
fact_bis:
Ngano morag basa nga plastik ang dikya sa baybayon?

Ang cnidarian walay bukog, humok ang lawas nga murag jelly, ug kadaghanan tubig — mao nga morag basa nga plastik kon maanod sa baybayon.

findings.note: title_bis "Lawas sa Labod" for "Jellyfish Body" — labod is a welt/wound mark in Cebuano (see ffct-13984 "Kon adunay samad o labod nimo"), not a jellyfish; the corpus's jellyfish words are dikya / salabay / bantol, and this card's own body uses dikya.

fact_en: Rats and mice are pests — they gnaw on food and household things, damaging them.
fact_bis: Ang ilaga ug ilagang gamay mga peste — ilang kutkoton ang pagkaon ug mga butang sa balay, mao nga madaot kini.

findings.note: title_bis "Ilaga ug Guya nga Peste" for "Rats and Mice as Pests" — guya is a CALF, not a mouse (same corpus uses it that way in ffct-06093, "usa lamang ka guya ang ipanganak" of a carabao). Title claims calves are household pests; body only says "ilaga ug ilagang gamay".

fact_en: When you're struggling with your feelings, you can turn to a parent, teacher, guidance counselor, or another trusted adult.
fact_bis: Kung naglisod ka sa imong pagbati, makaduol ka sa ginikanan, magtutudlo, guidance counselor, o ubang masaligang hamtong.

findings.note: title_bis "Tigulang nga Pangayo sa Tabang" for "Trusted Adults for Help": tigulang = elderly/old person, not adult (hamtong), and the phrasing reads as the old person asking for help rather than the child asking a trusted adult. The body correctly says "ubang masaligang hamtong", but the title changes who a struggling child is told to approach - on a socio-emotional safety card that swap matters.

fact_en:
What animal has true feathers?

Birds! Feathers cover their whole body, and birds are the only animals that have true feathers.
fact_bis:
Unsang mananap ra ang adunay tinuod nga balhibo?

Ang langgam! Ang balhibo nagtabon sa ilang tibuok lawas, ug sila ra ang mananap nga adunay tinuod nga balhibo.

findings.note: title_bis "Buhok nga Motabon sa Langgam" = "hair that covers the bird". The card's entire claim is that birds are the ONLY animals with TRUE FEATHERS (body correctly uses balhibo throughout), so the title header names a different thing than the fact it heads - buhok is head hair and is never feathers. A child scanning titles reads the feather-uniqueness card as being about hair.

fact_en:
What are an ant's antennae for?

A worker ant's two antennae work like its nose and hands — it uses them to smell, touch, and even 'talk' to other ants!
fact_bis:
Para unsa ang antennae sa langgam?

Ang duha ka antennae sa worker ant sama sa ilong ug kamot niini — gamiton niya kini aron makapanimaho, makahikap, ug makig-istorya sa ubang langgam!

findings.note: Card is about a worker ant's antennae, but the Cebuano question asks 'Para unsa ang antennae sa langgam?' and the answer ends '...makig-istorya sa ubang langgam!'. In Cebuano langgam = BIRD (the ant sense is Tagalog). A child reading only the Cebuano is told birds have antennae and use them to talk to other birds; the single mid-sentence English 'worker ant' does not undo the question and the closing clause, which both name the wrong animal.

fact_en:
Why are bird bones so light?

Human bones are packed with soft marrow that makes blood. A bird's hollow bones hold less marrow — one more reason birds weigh so little.
fact_bis:
Ngano gaan ang buto sa langgam?

Puno sa humok nga marrow ang buto sa tawo nga naghimo og dugo. Gamay ra ang marrow sa hawan nga buto sa langgam — mao nga sila gaan.

findings.note: title_en 'Hollow Bird Bones' became title_bis 'Wala Bukog Langgam', which in Cebuano reads 'birds have no bones' — the opposite of the card's fact that bird bones are hollow and hold less marrow. The body never repairs it because it never uses 'bukog': it says 'buto' three times ('gaan ang buto sa langgam', 'hawan nga buto sa langgam'), and 'buto' is not Cebuano for bone (that is Tagalog; Cebuano 'buto' = burst/explode, and is vulgar slang). So the false title claim stands uncorrected for a Cebuano-only reader.

fact_en: Your skin releases sweat to cool your body down when you're feeling hot or tired.
fact_bis: Ang panit magpagawas og singot aron pabugnawon ang lawas kon init o gikapoy kita.

findings.note: title_bis "Pagbahinbahin sa Pagpainit" (distributing/partitioning of heating) for title_en "Sweat Cools the Body" — the title states the opposite direction (pagpainit = causing heat) and never mentions singot. The body sentence is correct ("magpagawas og singot aron pabugnawon ang lawas"), so this is a title-only reversal.

fact_en:
What does Darwin's theory say about life?

According to Darwin's theory of evolution, all living things descended from common ancestors!
fact_bis:
Unsa ang giingon sa teorya ni Darwin bahin sa mga buhing butang?

Sumala sa teorya sa ebolusyon ni Darwin, ang tanang buhing butang naggikan sa managsamang katigulangan!

findings.note: title_bis "Darwin ug Kasingkasing Ninuno" for title_en "Darwin Common Ancestors": `kasingkasing` means heart, so the title reads "Darwin and the Heart Ancestor". Body correctly says "managsamang katigulangan", but the title names a different thing (heart) that has nothing to do with common descent.

fact_en: Many lymph nodes sit in the neck, armpits, and groin — that's why swelling is often felt there when you're sick!
fact_bis: Daghang lymph node ang naa sa liog, ilok, ug singit — mao nga didto kasagaran mabati ang pamaga kon masakit!

findings.note: Tapai card: EN says tapai is fermented from "rice or cassava"; bis says "gikan sa bigas o kamote". In Cebuano `kamote` is sweet potato, a different plant from cassava (balanghoy / kamoteng kahoy). Nothing else in the card corrects it, so a child learns the wrong source crop.

fact_en: The instant you slip, your body automatically throws out your arms to keep you from falling — before you even think about it!
fact_bis: Kung kalit ka madakin-as, awtomatik nga ituy-od sa imong lawas ang mga bukton aron dili ka matumba — sa dili pa nimo kini mahunahunaan!

findings.note: title_bis is "Reflex Braha Landslides" for title_en "Automatic Balance Reflex". `Landslides` names an unrelated phenomenon (dahili/landslide) and `Braha` is not a Cebuano word; the title tells the child the card is about landslides, not about the arm-out balance reflex the body describes (body text itself is correct).
